# MCP tools

<!-- BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED intro -->

The server has 12 tools, one per operation. It serves MCP [revision 2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro) and refuses every other revision.

<!-- END AUTO-GENERATED intro -->

Transport: streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:17952/mcp`.

> The intro and the tool tables are autogenerated from [source](../mcp-server/app) by `just generate_mcp_tools_doc`.

## Artifacts

| Tool                 | What it does                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `km_list_artifacts`  | List artifacts in the store, newest first.                                                             |
| `km_read_artifact`   | Read one artifact in full, including its instance records and any findings the store reports about it. |
| `km_create_artifact` | Create an artifact as a draft.                                                                         |
| `km_update_artifact` | Replace parts of an artifact.                                                                          |
| `km_delete_artifact` | Delete an artifact permanently.                                                                        |
| `km_commit_artifact` | Ask for an artifact to be committed, and relay the answer.                                             |

Each artifact tool takes an optional `vault` argument — an id from `km_list_vaults` — carried to
the engine as the `X-Km-Vault` header. Omitted, the engine's default vault answers. Reads return an
`etag`; updates require it and are refused if the underlying file changed.

## Files

| Tool            | What it does                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `km_list_files` | List every file in the vault content folders.   |
| `km_read_file`  | Read one vault file by its vault-relative path. |

File tools cover `+`, `x`, `Atlas`, `Calendar`, and `Efforts`. Artifact Markdown appears in both
the raw file and structured artifact views. Markdown content is inline; other file types return an
absolute local path for direct retrieval. Both tools accept the optional `vault` argument.

## Universes

| Tool                        | What it does                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `km_list_universes`         | List the universes this build carries.                                                                         |
| `km_read_universe`          | Read one universe in full: its elements, artifact types and their compositions, frames, factors and relations. |
| `km_read_universe_guidance` | Read a universe's guidance: how to answer each element and artifact type well, and what each value means.      |

Universes are engine-global — they describe how knowledge is structured, not where it lives, so
they take no `vault` argument.

## Vaults

| Tool             | What it does                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `km_list_vaults` | List the vaults the engine serves: id, name, path. |

## Receipts

Every successful request carries a `_request` receipt — method, URL, status, elapsed milliseconds,
the vault when one was named, and the response ETag when present.

## The acting party

The server declares itself an agent on every request. The engine records its writes as
`agent:knowledge-mcp`, refuses writes asserted in a person's name, and refuses commits — see
[how-writes-are-refused.md](how-writes-are-refused.md). A refused commit returns a structured
`personRequest` for execution through any trusted local client.
